responsibilities: Design, build and maintain governed semantic models and datasets
Create reusable business-ready data models built on Kimball and star-schema principles
Ensure data definitions are consistent, trusted and scalable across reporting, analytics and AI use cases
Establish and document core business metrics and definitions
Own standards around data quality, lineage, documentation and governance
Ensure reports, dashboards and AI tools return consistent answers from trusted data sources
Transform recurring requests into self-service, reusable analytical products
Reduce reliance on manual reporting and ad-hoc analysis
Drive automation of repetitive analytical processes using tools such as Power Automate
Prepare semantic models for Copilot, AI agents and natural-language querying
Create descriptions, metadata, guardrails and business context that improve AI-generated insights
Use AI tools to accelerate development, documentation and optimisation while applying rigorous validation and quality control
Set best practices for analytics engineering and data modelling
Mentor Analytics Engineers and support the wider data team
Partner closely with Data Engineering, Product and Commercial teams to deliver scalable solutions

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Use AI tools to accelerate development, documentation and optimisation while applying rigorous validation and quality control
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Governance vocabulary dominates - governed models, trusted definitions, data quality, lineage, documentation - and even the one acceleration bullet is immediately qualified by 'rigorous validation and quality control'.
evidence.domain_risk: Previous experience with procurement, spend, supplier or other complex master-data domains
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: A SaaS business whose data domains are procurement and supplier master data - errors affect business decisions but the JD invokes no regulatory, audit or financial-reporting obligation.
evidence.data_team_maturity: With a strong Data Engineering function already in place, they're looking for a Senior Analytics Engineer to own the semantic layer
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: A Data Engineering function and other Analytics Engineers already exist, but the semantic layer and metric governance are still to be established, so the function is growing rather than mature.
evidence.jd_authorship: Prepare semantic models for Copilot, AI agents and natural-language querying
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: The responsibilities name tools with precise application context - Power Automate for process automation, Copilot for semantic preparation, Kimball and star-schema for modelling - so the day-to-day is legible.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: own the semantic layer that sits between raw data and the insights, dashboards and AI tools relied upon across the business
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role's output is the modelling and semantic layer itself, consumed by reporting, self-service analytics and AI tools rather than aimed at one business function.
evidence.autonomy_level: Establish and document core business metrics and definitions
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role owns the semantic layer, establishes metrics and governance standards, and sets best practices for analytics engineering across the business.
evidence.ai_role: Prepare semantic models for Copilot, AI agents and natural-language querying
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate must build semantic models, metadata and guardrails that downstream AI agents consume, and also use AI tools in development - both signals present, so ai_enabler.
evidence.testing_framing: Own standards around data quality, lineage, documentation and governance
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Data quality standards are explicitly owned by the candidate as a named responsibility rather than appearing as a tool in the skills list.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Ensure reports, dashboards and AI tools return consistent answers from trusted data sources
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Trust and consistency dominate the responsibilities - 'consistent, trusted and scalable' definitions, 'governed' models - and the fear is inconsistent answers reaching reports, dashboards and AI tools.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Move the business from reactive reporting to productised, self-service analytics
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The role builds a new semantic layer and metric standards while also converting existing manual reporting and ad-hoc analysis into reusable products.
evidence.work_arrangement: Senior Analytics Engineer | Competitive Salary | Hybrid – Glasgow
evidence.loss_aversion: Ensure data definitions are consistent, trusted and scalable across reporting, analytics and AI use cases - the risk being controlled is divergent definitions producing inconsistent answers, particularly once AI tools query the semantic layer. Note: this is a recruitment agency posting for an unnamed SaaS client.
